summary: The root حوش (Hwsh) primarily describes something wild, untamed, or unfamiliar, like a wild animal or an unsociable person.
lane: حُوشِىٌّ ذ Wild; untamed; undomesticated; uncivilized; unfamiliar; syn. وَحْشِىٌّ . (S, Msb.) -b2- Applied to a man, (tropical:) Wild; uncivilized; unfamiliar; (A;) unsociable; that does not mix with others. (S, A.) -b3- Applied to a camel, or other [animal], Wild: (K:) [or] the epithet thus applied is tropical; (A, TA;) and what are thus called, (K,) or الإِبِلُ الحُوشِيَّةُ [ the camels termed حوشيّة ], (S, A, Msb,) are so named from , the appellation of certain stallions of the camels of the jinn, or genii, which covered some of the she-camels of Arabs, (IKt, S, A, Msb, K,) as they assert, (S, K,) namely, of the she-camels of Mahrah, (K,) meaning the Benoo-Mahrah-Ibn-Heydán, (TA,) and the offspring were the camels called النَّجَائِبُ المَهْرِيَّةُ , (Msb, TA,) which scarcely ever become tired; and the like of this is said by AHeyth: (TA:) it is also said that , (S, K,) from which the epithet above mentioned, thus applied, is a rel. n., (TA,) is the country of the jinn, (S, K,) beyond the sands of Yebreen, which no man inhabits: (S:) or an appellation of certain sons of the jinn, whose country is called بِلَادُ الحُوشِ by Ru-beh: (TA:) or it is like الوَحْش : (Msb:) or إِبِلٌ حُوشِيَّةٌ means camels of the jinn: or wild camels; (TA;) as also : (S:) or camels not completely broken or trained, because of their unyielding spirit. (TA.) -b4- Hence, (A,) رَجُلٌ حُوشِىٌّ الفُؤَادِ , (A,) or الفُؤَادِ , (S, K,) (tropical:) A man acute, or sharp, in intellect. (S, * A, K, * TA. *) -b5- You say also, كَلَامٌ حُوشِىٌّ (tropical:) Strange, uncouth, unusual, extraordinary, or unfamiliar, speech; such as is difficult to be understood; (Msb, K, TA;) i. q. وَحْشِىٌّ ; (S, A;) [opposed to فَصِيحٌ :] and in like manner, لَفْظَةٌ حُوشِيَّةٌ a word, or phrase, that is strange, uncouth, unusual, &c.; as also لَفْظَةٌ وَحْشِيَّةٌ , and غَرِيبَةٌ , and شَارِدَةٌ ; all opposed to لَفْظَةٌ فَصِيحَةٌ . (Mz, 13th نوع .) -b6- And لَيْلٌ حُوشِىٌّ (tropical:) A night that is dark (A, K) and terrible. (A, TA.)

headwords.def: حَاشَ الصَّيْدَ , (S, A, K,) aor. يَحُوشُ, (S,) inf. n. حَوْشٌ and حِيَاشٌ, (TA,) He came around the chase, or game, to turn it towards the snare; (S, A, K;) as also, and, (S, K,) inf. n. إِحَاشَةٌ and إِحْوَاشٌ. (TA.) حُشْتُ عَلَيْهِ الصَّيْدَ I aided him to hunt, or catch, the chase, or game; as also عليه, and عليه, and أَحْوَشْتُهُ إِيَّاهُ, on the authority of Th: (TA:) and حَاشَ عَلَيْهِ الصَّيْدَ He scared the chase, or game, towards him, and drove and collected it to him; as also.
(TA,) inf. n. تَحْوِيشٌ, (K,) He collected several things: or collected much. (K, * TA.) [See also 1.]

حاوش البَرْقَ He turned aside from the place of the rain of the lightning, whichever way it turned. (Ibn-'Abbád, K.) Hence, (TA,) حَاوَشَهُ, (A,) inf. n. مُحَاوَشَةٌ, (TA,) He circumvented him: or he endeavoured to induce him to turn, or incline, or decline; or endeavoured to turn him by deceit, or guile: syn. دَاوَرَهُ: (A, TA: *) in war, and in litigation or contention [&c.].
احاش الصَّيْدَ , and أَحْوَشَهُ: see 1, in five places.

تحوّش القَوْمُ عَنّى The people, or company of men, removed, withdrew, or retired to a distance, from me. (S, K. *) And تحوّش عَنِ القَوْمِ He removed, &c., from the people, or company of men. (TA.) تحوّشت مِنْ زَوْجِهَا She became forlorn of her husband; syn. تَأَيَّمَتْ. (Sgh, K.) تحوّش He felt, or had a sense of, or was moved with, shame, or shyness, or bashfulness. (AA, K.)

انحاش عَنْهُ He took fright, and fled from him; or was averse from him; and shrank from him; (S, * K;) and was frightened at him; and was moved by him. (TA.) [In the TA it is here added, that this verb is quasi-pass. of الحَوْشُ in the sense of النِّفَارُ; but this seems to indicate that a copyist has written النفار by mistake for الإِنْفَارُ, which is a syn. of the inf. n. of 1 in a sense explained above: so that انحاش signifies He became scared, or the like.] Hr mentions this verb in art.

احتوش القَوْمُ الصَّيْدَ , (S, Msb, K,) and, more commonly, بِالصَّيْدِ, (Msb,) The people, or company of men, encompassed, or surrounded, the chase, or game: (Msb:) or scared it, one, or one party, to another: (S, K:) the و remaining here unchanged as it does in اِجْتَوَرُوا. (S.) And احتوشو فُلَانًا (A, TA) They encompassed, or surrounded, such a one: (A:) or they made such a one to be in the midst of them; (TA;) as also احتوشوا عَلَيْهِ, (S, K,) [and احتوشوا حَوَالَيْهِ, (M and O in art.
حَاشَ لِلّٰهِ i. q. تَنْزِيهًا لِلّٰهِ. One should not say حَاشَ لَكَ, but حَاشَاكَ, and حَاشَى لَكَ. (S, K.) [See these phrases explained in art. حشى.]

A thing resembling [ the kind of enclosure, made of trees or of wood, &c, for camels or sheep or goats, called ] a حَظِيرَة: a word of the dial. of El-'Irák. (Sgh, K.) Applied by the people of Egypt to The court ( فِنَآء ) of a house: (TA:) [and to any court, or enclosure, surrounded by dwellings or the like, or by these and walls, or by walls alone: pl. of pauc. أَحْوَاشٌ, and of mult. حِيشَانٌ.]
: and الحُوشُ: see the next paragraph, in four places.

Wild; untamed; undomesticated; uncivilized; unfamiliar; syn. وَحْشِىٌّ. (S, Msb.) Applied to a man, (tropical:) Wild; uncivilized; unfamiliar; (A;) unsociable; that does not mix with others. (S, A.) Applied to a camel, or other [animal], Wild: (K:) [or] the epithet thus applied is tropical; (A, TA;) and what are thus called, (K,) or الإِبِلُ الحُوشِيَّةُ [ the camels termed حوشيّة ], (S, A, Msb,) are so named from, the appellation of certain stallions of the camels of the jinn, or…
[ Wildness; and the like; the quality of that which is termed حُوشِىّ:] (tropical:) unsociableness of disposition; or the quality of not mixing with others; in a man. (S.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
